title: Training Note — Collateral Protection Insurance When One Policy Covers Several Financed Vehicles
content:
**Rule.** Under Collateral Protection Insurance, where the product accepts one borrower policy listing several financed VINs, that one policy satisfies the insurance requirement of each listed contract, but it is reviewed and recorded separately on each contract's tracking record, and a VIN missing from the policy leaves that contract's record unsatisfied. Placed coverage, premiums and refunds belong to one tracking record and one contract only: premiums of different records are never combined, netted or billed to another contract, and a placement on one contract does not change the status of the borrower's other records.

## Questions the rule answers

**A borrower's single auto policy lists the VINs of two contracts financed with the company. How many reviews are recorded?** Two: one on each contract's tracking record. The policy can satisfy both contracts, but each record carries its own review.

**The same policy lists one financed VIN but not the other. What follows for the contract whose VIN is missing?** That contract's record is left unsatisfied by this policy; the listing of the other VIN does not carry over to it.

**Can a refund owed on one tracking record be set against a premium billed on another?** No. Premiums and refunds stay with their own record and contract; premiums of different records are never combined or netted.

**Coverage is placed on one of a borrower's contracts. Does that change the borrower's other tracking records?** No. A placement on one contract leaves the status of the borrower's other records as it is.

## The rule by object

| Item | Belongs to |
|---|---|
| Review of a policy listing several financed VINs | each listed contract's own tracking record, separately |
| Placed coverage | one tracking record and one contract |
| Premium charges | one tracking record and one contract; never billed to another contract |
| Premium refunds | one tracking record and one contract |
